paragraphs.title: Populating Jerusalem and the First Residents

easy.explanation: Nehemiah 11:1 says that the rest of the people cast lots.
easy.q: What did the rest of the people cast to decide who would dwell in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: One of ten was brought to dwell in Jerusalem.
easy.q: How many of the people were brought to dwell in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: The people blessed all the men who willingly offered themselves.
easy.q: What did the people do for the men who willingly offered themselves to dwell at Jerusalem?

answers: To bring one tenth of the people to Jerusalem
To choose a new high priest
medium.explanation: The lot determined which one of ten people would dwell in Jerusalem.
medium.q: Why were lots cast among the people?

answers: They were forced by the king
They were chosen because of their wealth
medium.explanation: The phrase describes people who volunteered to live in Jerusalem.
medium.q: What does the phrase “willingly offered themselves” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: The passage names certain children of Judah and Benjamin.
medium.q: Which two tribes are named among those dwelling in Jerusalem?

answers: It was considered worthy of honor
It was forbidden to most Israelites
It was only a duty for priests
challenge.explanation: Blessing the volunteers shows that their willingness was honored.
challenge.q: What does the people’s blessing of the volunteers suggest about dwelling in Jerusalem?

answers: They were four hundred sixty and eight valiant men
They were selected only by lot
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah 11:6 gives both their number and their description as valiant men.
challenge.q: What special detail is given about the sons of Perez who dwelt at Jerusalem?

answers: Joel was their overseer, and Judah was second over the city
Judah was their overseer, and Joel was second over the city
Sallu was their overseer, and Gabbai was second over the city
challenge.explanation: Joel was their overseer, while Judah was second over the city.
challenge.q: Who was the overseer of the children of Benjamin, and who was second over the city?

easy.explanation: The passage mentions singers and porters among the Levites.
easy.q: Which groups of Levites are specifically mentioned in the passage?

easy.explanation: Seraiah the son of Hilkiah was the ruler of the house of God.
easy.q: Who was the ruler of the house of God?

easy.explanation: The passage says that all the Levites in the holy city were two hundred fourscore and four.
easy.q: How many Levites were in the holy city?

answers: They had oversight of the outward business of the house of God
They were overseers of the city
They were chief rulers of Judah
medium.explanation: They had oversight of the outward business of the house of God.
medium.q: What responsibility did Shabbethai and Jozabad have?

medium.explanation: A ruler in this context was a person placed in authority over the house of God.
medium.q: What does the word “ruler” mean in the phrase “the ruler of the house of God”?

medium.explanation: The passage describes several organized duties in the service of the house of God.
medium.q: What different kinds of service are described among the priests and Levites?

answers: The servants were carefully organized and counted
They were not divided into different responsibilities
challenge.explanation: The numbers show that the servants and their duties were formally organized.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the numbers listed beside the various groups?

answers: Both groups served and dwelt in Jerusalem
Only the priests lived in Jerusalem
The Levites were rulers over Benjamin
challenge.explanation: The passage lists both priests and Levites who served in Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between the priests and the Levites in this passage?

answers: Zabdiel the son of one of the great men
challenge.explanation: Zabdiel was the overseer of the one hundred twenty and eight mighty men of valour.
challenge.q: Who was overseer of the mighty men of valour among the priests?

paragraphs.title: Temple Servants, the Levite Official, and Service to the King

easy.explanation: The passage says that the Nethinims dwelt in Ophel.
Uzzi the son of Bani was the overseer of the Levites at Jerusalem.
easy.q: Who was the overseer of the Levites at Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: The sons of Asaph were the singers and were assigned service in the house of God.
easy.q: What were the singers responsible for doing?

answers: He oversaw the Levites and the work of the house of God
He served beside the king in all matters
He appointed the children of Judah
medium.explanation: Uzzi was overseer of the Levites, who were responsible for the work of the house of God.

answers: They received an assigned portion each day
They sang only on feast days
They guarded the gates every night
medium.explanation: The king commanded that a certain portion should be provided for the singers each day.
medium.q: What does “due for every day” mean concerning the singers?

medium.explanation: Pethahiah served at the king’s hand in all matters concerning the people.
medium.q: Who was at the king’s hand in matters concerning the people?

answers: The priests and Levites were in the cities of Judah, while the Nethinims were in Ophel
The priests and Levites were in Ophel, while the Nethinims were in Judah
All of them dwelt only in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The passage places the remaining priests and Levites in Judah’s cities and the Nethinims in Ophel.
challenge.q: What difference is shown between the dwelling places of the remaining priests and Levites and those of the Nethinims?

answers: Uzzi oversaw the Levites and the work of the house of God, which included organized service such as singing
Uzzi was one of the kings
Uzzi replaced Pethahiah beside the king
challenge.explanation: Uzzi supervised the Levites’ work, while the singers served in the house of God.
challenge.q: How are Uzzi and the singers related in the organization of the service?

answers: Pethahiah served the people at the king’s hand
challenge.explanation: Pethahiah’s service concerned the people and the king, not only the Temple.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that service extended beyond the work of the house of God?

paragraphs.title: Settlements of Judah from the South to Jerusalem

easy.explanation: Beersheba and its villages are listed among the settlements of Judah.
easy.q: Which place is named among the settlements of Judah?

easy.explanation: The passage mentions Lachish and its fields, and Azekah and its villages.
easy.q: Which place is mentioned together with Lachish?

answers: From Beersheba unto the valley of Hinnom
easy.explanation: The passage says that they dwelt from Beersheba unto the valley of Hinnom.
easy.q: How far did the inhabited area extend?

answers: Smaller settlements associated with the towns and fields
Gates of the house of God
medium.explanation: The villages are listed alongside towns and their surrounding fields.
medium.q: What are “villages” in the context of these verses?

medium.explanation: Kirjath-arba, Dibon, and Jekabzeel are all listed among Judah’s settlements.
medium.q: Which sequence contains places named in the passage?

medium.explanation: The passage repeatedly mentions villages, fields, or villages thereof beside the towns.
medium.q: What do several of the towns have listed alongside them?

answers: It describes a broad distribution of towns, villages, and fields
It concerns only the house of God
challenge.explanation: The list covers many towns, villages, and fields across a wide area.
challenge.q: What does the list of places show about the settlement of Judah?

answers: They dwelt from Beersheba unto the valley of Hinnom
They dwelt only from Geba unto Bethel
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah 11:30 gives the range from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom.
challenge.q: What geographical statement summarizes the list?

challenge.explanation: Ziklag, Moladah, and Lachish appear in the list of Judah’s settlements.
challenge.q: Which group contains only places named among the settlements of Judah?

easy.explanation: Bethel and its villages are named among the settlements of Benjamin.
easy.q: Which city is named among the cities of Benjamin?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Lod, and Ono, the valley of craftsmen.”
easy.q: Which pair of places is mentioned together?

easy.explanation: The final verse mentions divisions of the Levites in Judah and Benjamin.
easy.q: What is mentioned at the end of the passage?

medium.explanation: Geba, Michmash, and Anathoth are listed among Benjamin’s settlements.
medium.q: Which list contains only places named among the settlements of Benjamin?

answers: Organized groups or sections of service
medium.explanation: Divisions refers to organized groups of Levites serving in the territories.
medium.q: What does “divisions” mean in the phrase “divisions in Judah, and in Benjamin”?

answers: From Judah’s settlements to Benjamin’s settlements and then to the Levites’ divisions
From Benjamin’s settlements to Judah’s lots and then to the kings
From the Temple to a list of kings
medium.explanation: The passage first lists Benjaminite towns and then concludes with Levitical divisions.
medium.q: How does the passage move from the preceding verses to its conclusion?

answers: Levitical service was connected with both Judah and Benjamin
The Levites lived only in Jerusalem
The Levites had no connection with the settlements
challenge.explanation: The final verse specifically places Levitical divisions in both Judah and Benjamin.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the Levites being mentioned after the list of Benjaminite settlements?

challenge.explanation: The valley of craftsmen is mentioned after Lod and Ono.
challenge.q: Which easily overlooked place appears among the towns of Benjamin?

challenge.explanation: Bethel is listed among Benjamin’s settlements, while Beersheba appears among Judah’s settlements.
challenge.q: Which pair contains one place from Benjamin’s list and one place from Judah’s list?
